generated.title: Why Does Earthquake Depth Matter?
generated.description:
Every earthquake begins at a point underground called the focus. Shallow earthquakes start within about 70 kilometers of the surface; deep ones can start hundreds of kilometers down.

Seismic waves spread out and weaken as they travel, so for the same magnitude a deep focus usually means weaker shaking at the surface, while a shallow focus puts the surface much closer and shaking can be violent. That's why shallow earthquakes can be especially damaging.

Depth isn't everything: magnitude, soil, and building quality matter too.

Part of the Earthquake Science Explained series. Subscribe to Next Huge Quake for more earthquake science.
